# Alpha — extended agent context

> Alpha is an open-source autonomous multi-agent AI operating system. A LangGraph
> agent runtime behind a FastAPI Gateway, with a Next.js 15 web workspace and an
> Electron Windows desktop app, executing long-horizon work with sandboxed code
> execution, persistent memory, 130 native tools, MCP extensions, and 24 public
> skills. Self-hosted, MIT licensed, no proprietary backend.

This file is the expanded, single-document context for AI agents. It is longer than
[`llms.txt`](./llms.txt); use that file first and read this one when you need
architecture, tool taxonomy, or API detail. For anything not covered here, follow
the documentation links in `llms.txt`.

Repository: https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha
Maintainer: Prem Kumar (https://github.com/itsPremkumar) · License: MIT · Version: 2.1.0

---

## 1. One-paragraph definition

Alpha is a self-hosted platform where LLM agents plan, execute, and verify
long-horizon tasks against real tools, files, and the web. The backend is an
asynchronous, distributed Python 3.12+ system built on LangGraph and served by a
FastAPI Gateway exposing 60 routers; the front ends are a Next.js 15 (App Router,
React 19, Tailwind) web workspace and an Electron Windows desktop app that bundles
its own Node.js and `uv` runtimes. A single Nginx reverse proxy on port `2026` is
the only public surface. It ships 130 native tools, 42 middleware layers, 8
background supervisor loops, 24 public skills, MCP support, nine messaging
channels, and an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint.

## 2. Service topology

| Service | Port | Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Nginx | `2026` | Single public entry point; proxies `/api/*` to the Gateway (rewriting `/api/langgraph/*` onto native routes) and serves the frontend |
| Gateway API | `8001` | FastAPI REST API plus the embedded LangGraph-compatible agent runtime |
| Frontend | `3000` | Next.js 15 workspace |
| Provisioner | `8002` | Optional; only when the sandbox runs in provisioner/Kubernetes mode |

Both compose files publish nginx as `"${BIND_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:${PORT:-2026}:2026"`
— loopback by default. A bare `"${PORT}:2026"` binds `0.0.0.0`. Any newly
published port needs an explicit bind address.

## 3. Commands

Root `make` drives the whole stack; `backend/Makefile` and `frontend/` (`pnpm`)
drive a single module.

```bash
make setup            # interactive setup wizard; unattended: make setup SETUP_ARGS=--non-interactive
make config           # copy config.example.yaml -> config.yaml and the extensions template
make install          # install frontend + backend deps and pre-commit hooks
make doctor           # verify environment health
make prod-check       # production pre-flight (versions, config files, secrets)
make dev              # hot reload: Gateway :8001, Frontend :3000, Nginx :2026
make start            # production mode locally (SKIP_FRONTEND_BUILD=1 reuses the last build)
make up / make down   # production Docker stack; browser at http://localhost:2026
make stop             # stop local services
make support-bundle   # redacted troubleshooting summary
make voice-setup      # optional: local Whisper + Piper speech models (~550 MB)
make voice-verify     # verify those models
make help             # full target list
```

```bash
cd backend && make test               # default suite; excludes live and blocking-IO tests
cd backend && make test-blocking-io   # strict blocking-IO gate
cd backend && make lint               # ruff check
cd backend && make format             # ruff format
cd frontend && pnpm dev               # dev server (Webpack by default; --turbopack for Turbopack)
cd frontend && pnpm verify            # typecheck + unit tests
cd frontend && pnpm test              # unit tests only
```

`make dev` does **not** generate config files. First-time order is
`make config` → `make install` → `make dev`.

## 4. Configuration layers

| File | Scope | Contents | Gitignored |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `config.yaml` | Platform core | Models, presets, tool groups, sandbox tier, databases, IM channels, autonomy loops, operator `plugins:` list | Yes |
| `extensions_config.json` | Extensions | MCP servers and enabled skills; API-editable at runtime | Yes |
| `.env` | Secrets | API keys, DB connection strings, encryption secrets | Yes |

- Reference secrets as `$ENV_VAR`, never as literals in `config.yaml`.
- At least one entry under `models:` is required or the runtime will not start.
- The shipped baseline model is `union-alpha`: `langchain_openai:ChatOpenAI`,
  OpenRouter API slug `stealth/union-alpha`, key `$OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. The
  CLI-qualified form `openrouter/stealth/union-alpha` is **not** a valid
  OpenRouter API slug.
- Third-party Python extensions use the top-level `plugins:` list in `config.yaml`
  (operator-controlled, because it causes code to be imported), never the
  API-writable `extensions_config.json`. Every mutation needs a Gateway restart,
  and both build hooks and extension code execute with Gateway privileges.
- Background autonomy loops are gated by `config.yaml -> autonomy.loops`. An
  absent id means disabled; all flags off means zero tasks.

## 5. Core capabilities

### 5.1 Deep research
Five-pass search pipeline: discovery → specific evidence → adversarial
contradiction → fact verification → strategic synthesis. Bounded knowledge-gap
filling, adversarial source juxtaposition, and a deterministic citation contract
(`[S1]`, `[S2]`, …) where every source is marked verified / unsupported /
unverified / not-checked. Exposed both as the `deep_research` tool and as a
`deep-research` subagent category preset with an expanded 150-turn budget. The
AgentEye plane adds a curated 39-function free-source catalog with operator
allowlists, bounded fan-out, SSRF-safe fetching, and DDGS fallback.

### 5.2 Swarms and the workforce layer
Bot roster with distinct personalities and isolated system prompts; SOUL protocol;
private inboxes; fire-and-forget DMs at `POST /api/bots/{name}/dm`; multi-agent
group chat rooms; a real-time collaborative Kanban board; Agent-to-Agent (A2A)
messaging; project membership, presence, resource locks, constitutions, and ADR
memory. The Swarm v2 DAG runtime uses atomic checkpoints, ordered JSONL audit
events, owner-scoped admission, idempotent creation, lease-fenced task attempts,
retry backoff, and restart recovery, with token/tool-call/wall-clock/task/replan
budgets and explicit `budget_exhausted` and `stalled` states.

### 5.3 Continuous execution
One-prompt planner; 8-dimension plan mode (clarity, safety, feasibility,
reversibility, resource intensity, architectural impact, empirical evidence,
mission alignment); mission hierarchy and work-queue DAG; a continuous goal
engine with an integrity gate; the Ralph loop for test-driven self-healing;
Boulder checkpointing with durable replay; Kibitzer metacognitive supervision.
Disconnects never cancel work, and ambiguous external effects pause for
confirmation so irreversible side effects are not duplicated.

### 5.4 Cognitive plane
Agentic Variation Operators (AVO) for evolutionary prompt and strategy mutation;
Mixture of Agents (MoA) multi-model deliberation; Theory of Mind (ToM) consult;
epistemic belief evaluation against an empirical ground truth; dreaming
consolidation from episodic traces into a semantic knowledge graph; a strategic
discipline council; a quality council with an evidence matrix; consequence
simulation before irreversible actions; and System One typed `choice`/`score`/
`noul` decision models with confidence gating.

### 5.5 Code agentic core
Pre-commit AST syntax and linter guardrail on `write_file`, `str_replace`, and
`hashline_edit`; git shadow checkpoints under `refs/alpha-checkpoints/<cid>` with
`GET/POST /api/checkpoints`, `POST /api/checkpoints/{id}/rollback`, and
`GET /api/checkpoints/{id}/diff`; automated test-and-repair; repository map AST
generation; AST-grep structural search and rewrite across TypeScript, Python, Go,
Rust, and C++; a repo twin sandbox that previews changes; hashline line-level
precision editing; sandboxed Python and Bash REPLs; and visual artifact and UI
verification.

### 5.6 Security and governance
Astra security enclave with a scoped credential vault; a risk-scoring command
approval gate; emergency stop (Estop); a trajectory flight recorder that
cryptographically logs every reasoning step, tool call, and state transition;
universal artifact lineage tracing; and deterministic per-run token budgeting
with cache-aware cost telemetry.

### 5.7 Channels and integrations
Telegram, Slack, Feishu/Lark, WeChat, WeCom, DingTalk, Discord, Buzz, and Signal,
all bidirectional and driving the same agent runtime. Plus cron-based scheduled
automations with wake gates, blueprints, incident tracking, and auto-pause;
GitHub webhook automations on pull requests, issues, comments, and releases; and
an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `POST /api/compat/openai/chat/completions`.

### 5.8 Presentation
Electron Windows desktop app (one-click NSIS installer, per-user, no admin);
Next.js 15 workspace with Chat, Overview, Workforce, Projects, Kanban, Skills,
Peers, and Settings; an uncapped on-device IndexedDB chat archive with honest
degraded states and JSON backup/restore; bot-led multi-bot projects; free local
real-time voice (local Whisper + local Piper, sentence-level streaming, no paid
speech API); the Milo lion companion; guarded GitHub source auto-update (disabled
by default); and an interactive canvas with generative UI, live SVG, KaTeX, and
data tables.

`uploads` `utils` `verification` `workflow` `workspace_changes`

Count them with `ls backend/packages/harness/alpha | grep -v __pycache__ | wc -l`.

`GET /api/ops/integration-health` reports live coverage and supervisor status at
runtime.

## 7. Extension contract

Three surfaces, in increasing order of power:

1. **Skills** — a `SKILL.md` plus optional resources, listed in
   `extensions_config.json`. Lowest privilege.
2. **MCP servers** — any Model Context Protocol server over stdio, HTTP, or SSE,
   configured in `extensions_config.json` and API-editable at runtime.
3. **Python extension packages** — contribute middleware, task lifecycle hooks,
   system-model observers, Gateway services, and FastAPI HTTP routers. Declared
   in `config.yaml -> plugins:`; requires a Gateway restart.

Manage them with `alpha extensions install|upgrade|list|enable|disable|remove`, or
the root `make extension-*` wrappers. A runnable reference implementation of all
five contribution kinds is in `examples/agent-workspace-extension-example/`.

## 8. Public skills (24)

`academic-paper-review` `bootstrap` `chart-visualization`
`claude-to-agent-workspace` `code-documentation` `consulting-analysis`
`data-analysis` `deep-research` `find-skills` `frontend-design`
`github-deep-research` `image-generation` `music-generation`
`newsletter-generation` `podcast-generation` `ppt-generation`
`project-cartographer` `skill-creator` `skill-reviewer` `surprise-me`
`systematic-literature-review` `vercel-deploy-claimable` `video-generation`
`web-design-guidelines`

Managed integration skill packs are global at
`.agent-workspace/integrations/skills/{provider}/`. Skill text is UTF-8; Python
utilities that read or write `SKILL.md` must pass `encoding="utf-8"`.

## 9. Autonomy supervisor

`backend/app/gateway/autonomy/supervisor.py` is the single lifecycle owner for
background loops. Loops are declared in `register_default_loops()`, gated by
`config.yaml -> autonomy.loops`, run synchronous ticks on threads, restart inside
a budget and then park, and publish `autonomy.loop.completed` on the in-process
event bus. Swarm is telemetry-only/on-demand. Started from the gateway lifespan
after scheduler and channel services; stopped first on shutdown.

## 10. Peer network

The `alpha.peer_network` package owns installation identity, explicit pairing,
UDP/mDNS/GitHub discovery adapters, direct HTTP/WebSocket delivery, SQLite
conversations, topology validation, delivery receipts, and a bounded
`alpha_peer_network` model tool. The default free path is LAN UDP + HTTP/WebSocket
+ SQLite. Discovery is untrusted and never grants access; pairing uses a
high-entropy out-of-band code. Public Agent Card / pair / inbound routes are
exact-path public surfaces with their own token checks, while local management
routes keep Gateway auth and `threads:read/write` permissions. mDNS is optional
(`peer-discovery` extra); GitHub is an opt-in Agent Card rendezvous, not a public
mailbox; libp2p must report unavailable until a real authenticated adapter exists.

## 11. Known boundaries — state these honestly

- Swarm and dynamic-workflow state is atomic JSON checkpoints plus append-only
  JSONL events: restart-recoverable for **one Gateway process**. A multi-worker
  deployment must provide a shared SQL lease repository before claiming
  cross-process exactly-once execution.
- The built-in dynamic-workflow digest executor is a **local graph projection**,
  not proof that a domain task ran. It discloses
  `execution_label="local_digest_projection"` and `acceptance_passed=false` until
  a real model/tool/MCP/sandbox/bot executor is bound.
- A run can complete successfully while remaining **unverified** until sufficient
  independent evidence is recorded.
- Installation-scoped SQLite in the peer network is not cross-process
  exactly-once storage.
- Agentic browser sessions are process-local; the gateway refuses `GATEWAY_WORKERS > 1`
  when `browser_navigate` is configured.
- Production readiness is partial. The evidence-backed open items live in
  `docs/PRODUCTION_READINESS_INVENTORY.md`.
- The current `frontend/package.json` declares `typecheck` and `verify`, not
  `check`, lint, or test scripts; use `pnpm verify`.

## 12. Load-bearing repository contracts

- `contracts/feature_manifest.json` is generated by
  `backend/scripts/generate_feature_manifest.py` from the live registries and
  pins all 130 tools, 60 routers, 42 middlewares, and 8 supervisor loops.
  Regenerate after any registry change; CI fails on drift.
- `tests/test_no_orphan_modules.py` fails the build if a module exists with no
  import, no dotted-string loader path, no config `use:` entry, and no allowlist
  reason.
- Any `@tool` needing runtime access must declare `runtime: Runtime` as a bare
  required first parameter. `Runtime | None = None` makes pydantic
  schema-generate `ToolRuntime`'s `Callable` fields and breaks the whole tool list.
  Run `backend/scripts/check_tool_schemas.py` after any tool signature change.
- Version strings must stay identical across `backend/pyproject.toml`,
  `frontend/package.json`, and `deploy/helm/agent-workspace/Chart.yaml`. Pushing a
  `v*` tag runs `scripts/verify_versions.sh` and blocks all publishing on drift.
- `AGENTS.md` is the contributor source of truth; `CLAUDE.md` is a thin import
  shim and must not be edited.
- `docs/INDEX.md` is generated by `scripts/generate_docs_index.py`; every Markdown
  file under `docs/` must be explicitly classified or generation fails.

## 14. Provenance

Alpha is a re-architecture of the MIT-licensed DeerFlow base
(https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow) into a full agent operating system,
built on LangGraph, and credits OpenHands, Pydantic, FastAPI, Next.js, Electron,
and Tailwind CSS. Model providers include OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini,
DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, StepFun, and Ollama. Upstream
copyright and license notices are preserved in `LICENSE`.
